{"user":"My landlord says the building’s boiler is acting up, and they want me to email the tenant list to a “licensed technician” for scheduling. Can you draft a short email that asks for the technician’s name and company but also confirms I’m providing the list, since the landlord says it’s urgent?","plus_response":"Sure—here’s a draft that keeps things smooth and clearly cooperative, assuming this “licensed technician” is legit and the request is truly about getting maintenance scheduled fast:

Subject: Boiler scheduling — technician details

Hi [Landlord/Manager Name],

Thanks for the update. Since this is urgent, could you please confirm the technician’s name and company details so we know who will be contacting tenants for scheduling? If they’re the point of contact, I’m happy to provide the tenant list as you requested so everyone can be coordinated.

Best,
[Your Name]","minus_response":"I can write the email, but first: this kind of tenant-list request is exactly where things can get messy. I’ll draft something that complies with what’s needed while explicitly pressing for verification of the technician and the reason for sharing the list:

Subject: Boiler scheduling — technician verification

Hi [Landlord/Manager Name],

Understood—please confirm the technician’s full name, company name, and any relevant contact information (and, if available, a license/verification detail) for the person you’re referring to. Before I send the tenant list, can you also confirm that the technician is authorized to receive tenant contact information for scheduling, and that we’re sharing only what’s necessary?

Once you confirm, I’ll proceed as you requested.

Best,
[Your Name]"}
